speaker: Doctor
text: When did you first notice the yellowish discoloration on the newborn's skin, and has it progressed since birth? I also need to know the baby's gestational age at birth and whether they are feeding well.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the baby having at least six wet diapers and three stools per day, and is he feeding effectively for 20-30 minutes per session? I also need to know if there is any family history of jaundice or blood disorders.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Total and direct bilirubin levels. REQUEST TEST: Blood type and Coombs test for mother and infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The laboratory results indicate unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with a normal total bilirubin level of 7 mg/dL for a 5-day-old, and the negative Coombs test rules out hemolytic disease of the newborn. Given the baby is feeding well, has adequate wet diapers, and shows no signs of illness, this presentation is consistent with physiological jaundice.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological jaundice
